thread:
izzy_support: Customer ACME-prod reported p99 jump on /v1/generate at ~02:10 UTC — p99 went from ~450ms to ~2.1s. Customer says it started after ~01:50 and is impacting SLAs.
marco_runtime: Ack. Any errors in logs? request ids?
izzy_support: Provided 3 request ids: req_6a1f, req_6a23, req_6a3b. They attached a timeline and a heap graph. I'll paste key snippets.
izzy_support: log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T02:03:12Z ERROR worker-12 OOM when allocating 128MB for KV cache growth, fallback to CPU swap, latency spike
2026-03-15T02:03:13Z WARN worker-12 kv_cache_size=1.6GB -> 1.85GB
2026-03-15T02:05:01Z INFO allocator: slab_compact triggered on worker-12
```
lee_sre: That reads like GPU memory pressure -> spill/host swap -> massive tail latency. Do we see fragmentation metrics or repeated small OOMs?
anya_eng: Looking at metrics: GPU mem utilization steady ~74% but free chunk fragmentation high (many small free spans). KV entries per session grew by 3x compared to baseline for these tenant models. We also see repeated allocator retries around 02:03-02:06.
marco_runtime: Could be KV growth due to long-running prefix sessions + no eviction. What is the KV policy for that customer's model? 
izzy_support: Customer uses chat-history retention=unbounded (they asked to keep full convo for legal reasons). They were on model redwood-7b-v2-q that has a larger KV footprint.
lee_sre: That's the smoking gun. Large KV + fragmentation + allocator returning small slabs -> OOMs cause slow path swaps, p99 spikes.
anya_eng: Quick mitigations: 1) apply soft KV cap per-session (eg limit to 512MB) 2) enable kv_eviction_policy=LRU for that tenant 3) bump allocator slab_size to larger buckets to reduce fragmentation 4) enable backpressure at ingress (reject/queue long sessions)
izzy_support: Customer is sensitive to losing history (legal). Can we propose a non-destructive workaround while we fix allocator?
marco_runtime: Yes: enable kv_trim_to_recent=last_n_messages=200 as a configurable policy — preserves recent convo while capping KV growth. Also enable periodic async slab_compact more frequently (every 5m) as a bridge.
anya_eng: I can push a runtime flag to the staging pool: `--kv-evict=LRU --kv-trim=200 --slab-compact-interval=300s` and monitor. Will need a quick canary rollout to ~5 instances.
deploy-bot: Planning rollout: staging -> canary(5) @marco_runtime requested. Triggered at 2026-03-15T03:20:00Z.
lee_sre: Also recommend immediate mitigation: move the tenant to a dedicated pool with larger GPU memory (p4d-like) or a variant with quantized KV (q2) to reduce footprint.
izzy_support: I'll ask customer if they can accept temporary recent-only retention or a brief dedicated pool move. csm_rita will help with contract/ops ask.
csm_rita: I'll message them, but likely they prefer retention. I'll offer dedicated pool for critical windows if they won't accept trim.
anya_eng: Action items: 
- anya_eng: push flag to staging + canary (ETA 40m)
- marco_runtime: prepare dedicated pool migration playbook + cost estimate (ETA 30m)
- lee_sre: prepare allocator param patch (increase slab buckets & aggressive compaction), will try hot patch if feasible (ETA 2h)
- izzy_support: collect full request traces + customer's consent for temporary session trim (ETA 15m)
marco_runtime: For repro locally: we can simulate with script to create many long sessions with repeated prefixes: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 500); do 
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-v2-q","history":[...lots of turns...],"max_tokens":64}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" &
done
```
Monitor `nvidia-smi` and `/metrics/allocator_fragmentation`.
lee_sre: If you run that, you'll see p95 stable but p99 blow up once fragmentation crosses threshold (~60% fragmented free spans).
izzy_support: Customer approved temporary `kv_trim=200` for next 24h while we patch.
anya_eng: Good. I'll start the canary. Posting quick checklist in case rollback needed: 
- canary monitor p95/p99 and mem_frag
- if p99 < 700ms after 3m, promote
- if OOM events continue, roll back and switch tenant to dedicated pool
marco_runtime: Note: need to record the exact kernel logs for postmortem: `allocator: slab_compact` timestamps, and the worker id. Also tag traces with `tenant=ACME-prod` for evals.
izzy_support: Thanks team. I'll update customer and keep thread posted. :thumbsup:
lee_sre: thumbs. keep @oncall looped if we hit repeated OOMs.
izzy_support: Closing loop: canary started, p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 580ms after kv_trim + LRU on canary. We'll schedule allocator patch next sprint but consider urgent hotfix if any regressions.
marco_runtime: Filing follow-up ticket for allocator rework and per-tenant KV quotas: INF-4852. Assigning to anya_eng + lee_sre.
